tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H19): Two-accumulator 2SM pair kernel for 256 < B <= 512: one pass over N = Bpad, judged in cycles against CUTLASS 256x192/256x256. Start from tc_pair.cu in r3-e2-tc-pair-kbs2 and keep tc_small (B <= 131) and the r3 pair (131 < B <= 256) exactly as they are. Build tc_pair2 for 256 < B <= 512: cluster of 2, cta_group::2, M = 256 W rows per pair, N1 = 256 and N2 = Bpad - 256 (Bpad = roundup(B, 16), so N2 is a multiple of 16 and N2/2 of 8) as two UMMAs per K = 8 step into two TMEM accumulators at columns [0, 256) and [256, Bpad); tcgen05.alloc 512 columns per CTA (1 CTA per SM by shared memory). Per CTA per k-block the shared memory holds 16 KB of W (its own 128 rows) and Bpad/2 emb rows laid out as 128 rows for UMMA1 (coordinate rank*128) followed by N2/2 rows for UMMA2 (coordinate 256 + rank*N2/2), loaded by two emb TMA boxes; the second B descriptor is the first plus 16 KB. Both idescs differ only in the N field; both accumulators' zero-init predicate uses the (i|j|k) != 0 rule per accumulator. Steps: (1) Probe first, in one container, cycles per k-block (clock64 span per CTA, %globaltimer for the clock) for kbs=1 with 3/4/5 stages at Bpad 384 and 464 and 3/4 stages at 512, plus kbs=2 with 2 stages, with real W from DRAM under the harness flush and evict_first on W; record MMA-ideal clk per k-block (2*128*Bpad*32/4096 per SM), the no-MMA feed-only time, and the resident-operand time for the same shapes, so each configuration is classified as MMA-, ingest- or chain-bound (H23/H24). (2) In the same probe run the CUTLASS tiles the kernel replaces (256x192 at 373/384, 256x256 at 449/512) and convert wall time x clock to cycles. (3) Ship the best configuration as the dispatch for 256 < B <= 512 (keep CUTLASS for B > 512), run_tests on all 16 workloads, record max |err| vs fp64 per B (must be <= 1.75e-3), and state the predicted portal time as max(1.05 x rented DRAM time, cycles / 1.55 GHz) plus the 11% underprediction seen at 192/211. Stretch only if the above is done: let the kernel take a batch-tile index (n0 offset in the emb coordinates and output columns) so E2 can reuse it; do not spend the session on L. Success: At 373/384/449/512 the kernel uses >= 20% fewer SM cycles than the CUTLASS tile it replaces in the same probe (target: <= 100k cycles at 384 and <= 125k at 512), passes 16/16 x 10 rounds with max |err| <= 1.75e-3, one launch, and the per-stage time at kbs=1 is within 15% of the MMA-ideal (chain floor hidden). Refuted if: The kbs=1 ring at N >= 384 still shows a per-stage time pinned near the 551-674 clk floor or above the MMA-ideal by more than 30% at every stage count, or cycles are within 10% of CUTLASS's at all four sizes. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H22): L band: the two-accumulator pair kernel with two batch tiles of N <= 464 per W tile (grid of 144 pairs), vs CUTLASS 256x192 in cycles. Target 512 < B <= 919; keep every other path as in r3-e2-tc-pair-kbs2. Check the archive first with get_kernel for an E1 kernel of this round (two-accumulator tc_pair2); if it exists, branch from it, otherwise build the same core described in E1 (cluster 2, cta_group::2, N1 = 256 + N2 into two TMEM accumulators, Bpad/2 emb rows per CTA, kbs=1 with 4-5 stages, evict_first on W, TFLOAT32 maps). Add a batch tile dimension: nb = 2, Ntile = roundup(ceil(B/2), 16) (691 -> 352, 773 -> 400, 853 -> 432, 919 -> 464), grid = 72 W tiles x 2 batch tiles = 288 CTAs in 144 clusters, cluster id -> (W tile = id / 2, batch tile = id % 2) so the two tiles of one W tile launch adjacently and the second reads W from L2; emb coordinates are offset by n0 = tile * Ntile with TMA zero-fill beyond B; output stores guard n0 + col < B. Measure in one container, with real W under the harness flush, cycles per CTA (clock64 + %globaltimer) and harness_time at 691/773/853/919 for: (a) the new kernel, (b) the same with the batch-major cluster order (tile = id / 72) to test the L2 sibling-sharing assumption, (c) CUTLASS 256x192 (and 256x256 at 691) as shipped. Also try nb = 3 at 919 (320 columns per tile) once. Record for each: cycles, MMA-ideal cycles (2 passes x 96 x 2*128*Ntile*32/4096), the implied per-clock efficiency, max |err| vs fp64 (<= 1.75e-3) and DRAM bytes if the W sibling sharing fails (W read twice). Ship the best variant as the dispatch for B > 512, run_tests 16/16, and state the predicted portal time per the r3 rule. Success: >= 15% fewer SM cycles than CUTLASS 256x192 at 773/853/919 and >= 10% at 691 in the same probe, i.e. per-clock efficiency >= 85% of the UMMA rate over two passes, 16/16 x 10 rounds, one launch; the W-tile-adjacent order beats the batch-major order (W sibling read from L2). Refuted if: The one-pass N = 352-464 tiles show the same ~73-75% efficiency as CUTLASS (cycles within 8%), which would mean the ceiling is not per-SM ingest (H24) and the L band stays on CUTLASS. Experiment E3 (tests H24): Probe: per-SM TMA ingest ceiling and commit floor at N >= 384 stage sizes, and how both scale with the SM clock. Probe-only session; no candidate kernel is required. Reuse the r3-e2 microbenchmark harness (resident / L2-fed / DRAM-fed 2SM rings with clock64 and %globaltimer, barrier-trap on hang). Step 1 (H23 at large stages): resident operands, 2SM cta_group::2, one 1-k-block stage = 4 K-steps x two UMMAs (N1 = 256 and N2 = 128 / 208 / 256, two accumulators), commit per stage, 3/4/5 rotating stages: report clk per k-block against the MMA-ideal (768 / 928 / 1024) and against the 4-UMMA floor measured in the same container (N = 192 single accumulator). Step 2 (H24 ceiling): L2-fed ring (hot W tile shared by all CTAs), no MMA, stage bytes per CTA of 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 64 KB at kbs = 1 with 4 stages, and 48 / 64 / 96 KB at kbs = 2: clk per stage -> B/clk per SM; then the same stages with the MMA enabled: report whether time = max(MMA, feed) or closer to the sum. Step 3 (clock scaling): run the fed ring with MMA (N = 256 + 128, kbs = 1, 4 stages) in short bursts (~1.9 GHz) and after a sustained 60-90 s tensor-core loop that drives the card into the power cap (1.2-1.4 GHz, as r2-e3 did, reading the clock from globaltimer); report B/clk per SM and per-clock MMA efficiency at both clocks for the fed ring and for CUTLASS 256x192 at B = 384 (wall x clock). Step 4: 3 interleaved rounds for every number; one table per step with the clock noted. State in the findings which bound (MMA, chain, ingest) each configuration hits and the ingest ceiling in GB/s per SM at each clock. Success: Step 1 shows per-stage time within 10% of the MMA-ideal for N >= 384 (floor hidden); step 2 shows a feed-only ceiling in the 50-70 B/clk range that is independent of stage size above 32 KB; step 3 shows the ceiling in B/clk rising by >= 15% at the low clock (bytes-per-second ceiling), which supports H24 and predicts a portal/rented ratio below 1.31 for ingest-bound paths. Refuted if: Feed-only B/clk per SM scales with stage size or exceeds 90 B/clk (then the pair kernels at 192/256 were bound by something else), or the B/clk ceiling is the same at 1.3 and 1.9 GHz (ceiling in bytes per SM-clock: ingest-bound kernels would scale with the full 1.31 clock ratio at the portal and the E1/E2 gains would transfer unchanged, not improved).
